summary: TURP with spinal requested, but the patient stopped warfarin 2 days late (thought it was 3 days like his colonoscopy) and the INR is 1.9.

asa.rationale: Persistent AF on anticoagulation, CKD 3a, age 77.

decision.rationale: INR 1.9 contraindicates a spinal (needs normalization) and is high for a TURP. Delay 1 to 2 days with repeat INR rather than switch to GA, since the surgeon prefers spinal and bleeding risk applies either way. Discuss with urology.

redFlags.evidence: Last warfarin 10/23 (not 10/21); INR 1.9 this morning; anticoag clinic call 10/26 documented the error.
redFlags.action: No spinal until INR normalizes (under 1.5); delay and recheck.

redFlags.evidence: Retention with diphenhydramine, confusion with oxybutynin.

redFlags.implication: Saline lowers TURP syndrome hyponatremia risk but volume overload remains.
redFlags.action: Track irrigation deficit; spinal allows mental status monitoring.

redFlags.finding: AF with pauses and bradycardia history
redFlags.evidence: Holter pauses 2.2 s; HR 42 under propofol 2022; metoprolol taken.

planItems.item: Cefazolin 2 g within 60 min (childhood penicillin rash)
Inpatient with CBI; restart warfarin per urology
